recent_violations.inspector_comments: A MACHINERY ROOM.                                     18-28-1105.1 ACCESS THE MACHINERY ROOM SHALL BE RESTRICTED TO AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL.  A SIGN SHALL BE POSTED ON THE MACHINERY ROOM DOOR PROHIBITING ACCESS BY OTHERS.                                            18-28-1105.5 REFRIGERANT DETECTOR: MACHINERY ROOMS SHALL CONTAIN A REFRIGERANT DETECTOR WITH AN AUDIBLE AND VISUAL ALARM, THE DETECTOR OR SAMPLING TUBE THAT DRAWS AIR TO THE DETECTOR SHALL BE LOCATED IN AN AREA WHERE REFRIGERANT FROM A LEAK WILL CONCENTRATE.  THE ALARM SHALL BE ACTIVATED AT A VALVE NOT GREATER THAN THE CORRESPONDING TLV-TWA VALVE SHOWN IN TABLE 18-28-1103.1.  AUDIBLE ALARMS SHALL BE PLACED DIRECTLY OUTSIDE THE MACHINERY ROOM.  VISUAL ALARMS SHALL CONSIST OF A FLASHING YELLOW LIGHT PLACED DIRECTLY OVER THE MACHINERY ROOM DOORS WITH A SIGN THAT STATES "DANGER DO NOT ENTER WHEN LIGHT IS FLASHING, "PELIGRO NO ENTRA CUANDO LA LUZ ESTE."      18-28-1105.8 MACHINERY ROOMS SHALL BE MECHANICALLY VENTILATED TO THE OUTDOORS.  MECHANICAL VENTILATION SHALL BE CAPABLE OF EXHAUSTING THE MINIMUM QUANTITY OF AIR BOTH AT THE NORMAL AND EMERGENCY CONDITIONS.  MULTIPLE FANS OR MULTI SPEED FANS SHALL BE ALLOWED IN ORDER TO PRODUCE THE EMERGENCY VENTILATION RATE AND TO OBTAIN A REDUCED AIR FLOW FOR NORMAL VENTILATION.  PROVIDE:  A MACHINERY ROOM                            18-28-1105.8.2 MAKE-UP AIR.  PROVISIONS SHALL BE MADE FOR MAKE-UP AIR TO REPLACE THE AIR THAT IS BEING EXHAUSTED. recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: CHICAGO'S DEPARTMENT OF BUILDINGS REQUIRE A DETAILED AND COMPREHENSIVE CONDITIONS ASSESSMENT REPORT THAT ADDRESSES THE ENTIRE BUILDING SYSTEM AS OUTLINED WITHIN THE VIOLATION (EXAMPLE: THE ENTIRE EXTERIOR WALL OR THE ENTIRE PARKING STRUCTURE, ETC.), AND NOT LIMITED TO ONLY THE AREAS OUTLINED IN THE VIOLATION'S NOTES.  THE CAUSE AND POTENTIAL SOLUTIONS WITH FOCUS ON THE STRUCTURAL FOR DAMAGED AND DETERIORATED BUILDING COMPONENTS ARE REQUIRED.  IF THE PROFESSIONAL¿S OPINION IS THAT THERE ARE NO STRUCTURAL ISSUE, THEN THEY WILL NEEDS TO REPORT WHAT THEY BELIEVE CREATED THE APPEARANCE, EXPLAIN WHY THE CONDITION DOES NOT REQUIRE REPAIRS AND PROVIDE THE TECHNICAL PRINCIPLES, INDUSTRY STANDARDS AND DATA TO SUPPORT THE OPINION.  WHEN A PROFESSIONAL DISAGREES WITH ANY VIOLATION, THAT PROFESSIONAL MUST PROVIDE PROOF AS WELL AS ACCEPT LIABILITY FOR THE VIOLATIONS RELATED TO THEIR PROFESSIONAL OPINION. REPORT SHALL BE SIGNED AND SEALED BY AN ILLINOIS REGISTERED DESIGN PROFESSIONAL, AND BASED ON A CRITICAL, COMPREHENSIVE, AND DETAILED PHYSICAL INSPECTION OF THE PREMISES IDENTIFIED AND DETAILED IN THE VIOLATION - THE REPORT MUST IDENTIFY THE DATE, NATURE, SCOPE, FINDINGS, AND DEFICIENCIES OF THE INSPECTION/INVESTIGATION - THE REPORT MUST IDENTIFY EACH TECHNICAL PRINCIPLE OR STANDARD THAT IS THE BASIS OF ANY PROFESSIONAL JUDGMENT AND COMPREHENSIVE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR REPAIRS EXPRESSED IN THE REPORT - RECOMMENDATION OF REPAIRS MUST INCLUDE PHOTOS, DRAWINGS, DETAILS, AND CALCULATIONS WHICH MAY BE USED TO SUBMITTED FOR A REPAIR PERMIT WHEN ALLOWED - THE CONDITION REPORT, PERMIT, AND PERMITTED DRAWINGS MUST BE KEPT ON FILE AT THE PROPERTY AND MADE AVAILABLE FOR FIELD INSPECTION REVIEW AND APPROVAL BY ALL RELATED TRADES

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.
